changes: original_meaning 按古英语 styrian 的 gloss 收为「使动起来；搅动」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 按 Etymonline 编年（14 世纪初情感义、1540 年代 stir up 的煽动义）写明物理→情感的统一语义核，替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "Old English styrian, stirian \"to move, be or become active or busy, pass into motion,\" also transitive, \"to agitate with a rotating motion (a liquid or mixture by hand or with an instrument), move, change the location of; rouse, agitate, incite, urge\""
Etymonline: "By late 12c. as \"be alive;\" from early 14c. as \"affect emotionally.\" To stir up is from mid-14c. in a literal sense; by 1540s as \"rouse to action.\""
stir.mechanism_sentence: stir 是古英语 styrian「动起来、搅动」：锅里的汤要它搅，14 世纪起人心的情绪也被它「搅」动，煽动人群的 stir up 用的还是同一只手——让不动的东西动起来。

semantic_path.how: 『搅』从锅里走到心里：以旋转搅动液体就是今天的『搅拌』；14 世纪初添『触动情感』义，stir up 1540 年代添『煽动、激起行动』义——三件事共用一个核：让静止的东西动起来（Etymonline 编年）。

changes: original_meaning 按古英语 strūtian 的 gloss 收为「僵硬地突出，鼓起」。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 编年重建三站（突出 → 14 世纪末招摇/1510 年代阔步 → 1580 年代支柱），how 并陈名词来历的两说。
evidence: Etymonline: "strut (v.) \"walk in a vain, important manner, walk with affected dignity,\" 1510s, from Middle English strouten \"display one's clothes proudly, vainly flaunt fine attire\" (late 14c.), earlier \"to stick out, protrude, bulge, swell,\" from Old English strutian \"to stand out stiffly, swell or bulge out\""

Etymonline: "strut (n.1) \"supporting brace,\" 1580s, perhaps from strut (v.), or a cognate word in Scandinavian (compare Norwegian strut \"a spout, nozzle\") or Low German (compare Low German strutt \"rigid\")"
strut.mechanism_sentence: strut 的老底是「僵硬地挺出来」：挺着胸脯走，是「昂首阔步」（1510 年代）；挺着身子顶住结构的，是「支柱」（1580 年代）——一个「挺」字，两副面孔。

semantic_path.how: 『鼓出来显摆』走成了步态：中古 strouten 先指凸出、鼓起，14 世纪末添『穿着华服招摇炫耀』，1510 年代定型为动词『神气十足地大步走』——胸脯挺出去走路，就是 strut。
名词『支撑杆』1580 年代出现，来历两说并陈：或与动词同源（挺立顶住之物），或来自斯堪的纳维亚语、低地德语的同源词（Etymonline）——无论哪路，『挺、撑』的老核没变；词库『支柱』即此。

changes: original_meaning 保留拉丁语 stupidus 的 gloss「被击得失去知觉的；惊呆的」，并写明其词源结构（stupere 的派生、词根为『敲打』）。
semantic_path 第二站 how 写明 1540 年代入英语即指迟钝、而『惊懵』老义延续至 18 世纪中的编年事实，替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "stupid (adj.) 1540s, of persons, \"mentally slow, lacking ordinary activity of mind, dull, inane,\" from French stupide (16c.) and directly from Latin stupidus \"amazed, confounded; dull, foolish,\" etymologically \"struck senseless,\" from stupere \"be stunned, amazed, confounded,\" from PIE *stupe- \"hit,\" from root *(s)teu- (1) \"to push, stick, knock, beat\""

Etymonline: "Stupid long retained its association with stupor, and its sense of \"having the mind or faculties blunted or dulled, struck with stupor, dumbfounded\"... is attested by 1610s (OED pronounces it \"Very common in Dryden\") and lasted into mid-18c."
stupid.mechanism_sentence: stupid 在拉丁语里是「被击懵的」（词根是敲、打）：1540 年代入英语指人脑子迟钝，但「惊得发懵」的老味一直留到 18 世纪中——笨，最初是被打出来的状态，后来才成了天性。
stupid.original_meaning: 被击得失去知觉的；惊呆的

semantic_path.meaning: 被击得失去知觉的；惊呆的

semantic_path.how: 从『一时懵』沉淀成『天生笨』：1540 年代 stupid 入英语即形容人『心智迟钝』；只是它与昏厥的血缘断得慢——1610 年代至 18 世纪中它仍常指『惊、悲得发懵』。词库今义『愚蠢的』是前者胜出后的结果。

changes: original_meaning 前溯到拉丁语 succedere 的 gloss「紧接着来；接替」，并写明构词（sub- 紧贴 + cedere 走）；现行首站只到古法语。
semantic_path 第二站 how 依 Etymonline 明文（succeed well 的副词省略、15 世纪初结果义、约 1500 年指人成功）写明这条著名的语义省略，替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "succeed (v.) late 14c., succeden, intransitive and transitive, \"come next after, follow after another; take the place of another,\" especially \"be heir to, be successor to\"... from Latin succedere \"come after, follow after; go near to; come under; take the place of,\" also \"go from under, mount up, ascend,\" hence \"get on well, prosper, be victorious.\" This is from sub \"next to, after\" + cedere \"go, move\""

Etymonline: "In reference to deeds or dealings, the sense of \"turn out well, arrive at a happy issue, have a favorable result, terminate according to desire\" in English is by early 15c., with ellipsis of adverb (succeed well). Of persons, \"to be successful,\" from c. 1500."
succeed.mechanism_sentence: succeed 是拉丁语「紧贴着在后面走来」（sub- 紧贴 + cedere 走）：先是「接替、继承」；15 世纪 succeed well 里的 well 被省掉，「办得成」就直接成了「成功」。

semantic_path.how: 一个副词的省略造就了今义：拉丁语里 succedere 已兼有『进展顺利、兴旺』的引申；英语 15 世纪初 succeed well『（事情）办得顺』，well 渐被省去，动词单独扛下『结果圆满』，约 1500 年又落到人身上——『取得成功』（Etymonline 明言 ellipsis of adverb）。词库双义『成功；继承』正分属新旧两站。
